seo.title: Accessible New Zealand Tours for Blind Travellers | Watchout Tours
seo.description: Guided tours across New Zealand in groups of 6 at most, designed for blind and visually impaired travellers. Sensory experiences, independence, adventure and local connection.

masAlla.heroImgAlt: The Pōhutu geyser at Te Puia, Rotorua, sending a column of hot steam into a blue, cloud-streaked sky, beside a turquoise thermal pool surrounded by native bush

hero.eyebrow: Sensory trips through New Zealand for blind and low-vision travellers
hero.sub: Two guides, with you from start to finish. No limits.

viajes.title: Lived through your hands, your ears and your skin
viajes.p1: New Zealand is far away. But it doesn’t have to feel out of reach.
viajes.p2: We’ve designed experiences so that blind and low-vision people can discover this country with safety, independence and excitement.
viajes.p3: Feeling the breeze and cold water on your face at Milford Sound. Sensing the geothermal heat of Rotorua. Running your hands over the carvings of Māori designs. Stepping through the door of Bilbo’s house and into Hobbiton like a real hobbit.
viajes.p4: And this is only the beginning.
viajes.p5: Because the best way to get to know New Zealand isn’t always with your sight, but with all your senses.
viajes.fotoAlt: Two travellers sitting in a yellow kayak on the waters of Kaikōura, wearing Seal Kayak Kaikoura life jackets, looking towards another kayak with more travellers under a clear sky

explorar.title: Our way of exploring New Zealand
explorar.sub: We set no limits on adventure. Every route blends adrenaline, sensory immersion and authentic Māori culture.
explorar.p1Text: Paragliding in Queenstown, kayaking in Kaikōura, jet boats. No limits except the ones you set.
explorar.p2Text: Touch, smell and hearing as your guide: Hobbiton, Rotorua, Milford Sound, Te Puia.
explorar.p3Text: The moko, the hāngi, the song of the whales through a hydrophone in Kaikōura.

cultura.caption: The hāngi, the moko, the haka: Māori culture is lived up close, not watched from a distance.
cultura.fotoAlt: Young Māori man performing a haka at a cultural show, wearing a traditional bone necklace and piupiu skirt, pulling out his tongue in a ceremonial gesture of challenge

reel.videoAria: Video: one of our blind travellers takes off paragliding over Queenstown. He runs towards the edge of the slope, jumps and feels the thrill of touching the sky for the first time.
reel.eyebrow: This is how the adventure feels
reel.callout: Who said paragliding was only for some people?
reel.p1: At Watchout we believe adventure knows no limits. It knows curiosity, excitement, and people eager to throw themselves into experiences they’ll remember for a lifetime.
reel.p2: This is one of our travellers flying over Queenstown. The wind on your face, the sense of freedom and that mix of nerves and excitement right before take-off… some moments stay with you forever.

rutas.title: Two ways to live it
rutas.sub: Same route, you choose your format: in a group of 6 at most, with set dates, or private and at your own pace.
rutas.anuncioTexto: A small group of 3 to 6 travellers exploring New Zealand for 15 days. Spots are held on a first-come basis — tell us you’re in and we’ll save yours.

formatos.etiqueta: 15 days across New Zealand · group of 3 to 6 travellers + the two of us
formatos.cuerpo: A group of 6 travellers at most, with the same eagerness as you to explore the world. Over 15 days we’ll travel New Zealand together, sharing adventures, laughter and moments you’ll remember for a lifetime. Because some trips end… and others give you friendships forever. We’ll be by your side every step of the way, from the first day to the last.
formatos.incluye: Accommodation, all activities, transport during the route, the meals indicated, and the two of us with you for all 14 nights.

formatos.etiqueta: Private · just for you and yours · length at your own pace
formatos.cuerpo: A trip designed just for you, and for whoever you want to bring along. The two of us, exclusively, designing it at your pace: your days, your energy, your time. If you want more calm, more calm. If you want more adrenaline, more adrenaline. There’s no mould here. There’s a trip we make to measure, like a tailored suit.
formatos.incluye: Accommodation, all activities, transport during the route, the meals indicated, and the two of us with you from start to finish.

finalCta.p2: Write to us. We’ll answer your questions and figure out together which option fits you best.

seo.title: 60+ Journeys around New Zealand in groups of 6 at most | Watchout Tours
seo.description: Fifteen days around New Zealand at an easy pace, in groups of 6 at most, with private experiences, 4 and 5-star hotels, breakfast and dinner included and two dedicated guides throughout.

sinPrisa.heroImgAlt: The Pōhutu geyser at Te Puia, Rotorua, sending a column of hot steam into a blue, cloud-streaked sky, beside a turquoise thermal pool surrounded by native bush

hero.eyebrow: 60+ Journeys · New Zealand with all your senses
hero.h1: The trip you’ve been promising yourself for years.
hero.sub: Fifteen days around New Zealand in a group of 6 at most, at an easy pace, with Moni and Sylvie by your side from the moment you land to the last hug at the airport.

paraQuien.title: Who it’s for
paraQuien.p1: For anyone who has always dreamed of going to the other side of the world and has never found the right time, the right company or the energy to organise it. For couples who finally have the time, for groups of friends who’ve been saying “one day” for years, and for solo travellers who’d like to come home with new friends.
paraQuien.p2: You don’t need to worry about language, luggage, timetables or who to have dinner with. We take care of all that.
paraQuien.imgAlt: Three people stand beneath tall redwood trees, arms raised to touch a low branch as light filters through the canopy

incluye.title: What’s included
items: Moni and Sylvie with you for all 15 days.
Breakfast and dinner every day, plus lunch on many days.
Private experiences, just for the group.
Comfortable transport throughout and the domestic flight between the islands.

privado.title: Almost everything, just for you
privado.p: At Hobbiton, you explore the Shire with a guide for your group and have lunch at the Green Dragon Inn. In Rotorua, a Māori guide spends the whole day with you. In Auckland, you sail the harbour on a yacht that’s yours for the afternoon. No queues, no waiting for forty other people, and all the time in the world for questions.
privado.imgAlt: Young Māori man performing a haka at a cultural show, wearing a traditional bone necklace and piupiu skirt, pulling out his tongue in a ceremonial gesture of challenge

solo.title: Travelling solo
solo.p: Plenty of people travel with us on their own, and within a couple of days they’re part of the group. You can have your own room or, if you prefer, share with another solo traveller in the group.
solo.imgAlt: A woman rests her hand on a carved Māori figure while a companion beside her gestures as he describes it

familia.title: For your family
familia.p: Moni and Sylvie have lived in New Zealand for eight years and are with the group every single day, with 24-hour support. Your family can relax: you’re with us.
familia.imgAlt: Sylvie and Moni, Watchout Tours guides, smiling in front of a steaming geyser in Rotorua

momentos.texto: A relaxed breakfast at the hotel. We head south through green hills dotted with sheep.
Mid-morning we reach Hobbiton, where a guide is waiting just for our group to take us through the Shire. Lunch at the Green Dragon Inn, dessert included, with no one watching the clock.
In the afternoon, an easy drive to Rotorua, where the air already smells of sulphur.
Dinner at the hotel, then time to rest.

llevaras.title: What you’ll take home
llevaras.p: Steam from the geysers on your skin. Whale song through a hydrophone in Kaikōura. The stars of Tekapo, told around a campfire. The taste of hāngi, cooked underground on volcanic stones.

items.alt: Hobbiton, Matamata: hobbit holes set among green hills
Seven travellers and guides gather on a boardwalk with steam from the Pōhutu Geyser rising behind them
Milford Sound: sheer rock walls rising straight out of the fiord
Lake Tekapo’s turquoise water with mountains behind
Two travellers sitting in a yellow kayak on the waters of Kaikōura, wearing Seal Kayak Kaikoura life jackets, looking towards another kayak with more travellers under a clear sky

items.q: What if I’ve never done such a long trip?
items.a: Many of our travellers hadn’t either. We help you choose your flights and stopovers, and we’ll be waiting for you at Auckland airport.

items.q: Do I need to be fit?
items.a: There are short walks most days, always at an easy pace with plenty of breaks. If you’re unsure about anything, give us a call and we’ll talk it through.
International flights (we’ll help you book them) and travel insurance, which is compulsory.

items.q: What if I fancy something a bit more lively?
items.a: We can arrange optional extras: a helicopter flight over the glacier, a jet boat ride in Queenstown and a few more.

finalCta.title: Shall we talk?
finalCta.p: Tell us what you have in mind and we’ll answer all your questions, no strings attached.

seo.title: About Us | Mónica and Sylvie — Watchout Tours
seo.description: We’re Mónica and Sylvie, Spanish guides based in New Zealand. We create sensory, accessible trips for blind and low-vision travellers. This is our story.

sobre.heroImgAlt: Mónica and Sylvie smiling in a selfie by Sydney Harbour at dusk, with the Sydney Opera House in the background
sobre.heroIntro1: Watchout was born from the desire to create experiences where blind or visually impaired people can discover New Zealand from a more sensory, human and authentic place.
sobre.heroIntro2: But it’s also born with another purpose: to help open conversations, raise awareness of the invisible and spark new ways of travelling that people want to share.
sobre.aprendidoTitulo: Before starting this adventure we thought we were creating accessible trips. Today we know it’s much more than that.
sobre.aprendidoCol1: Every trip reminds us that there are many ways of perceiving the world. When we share those ways of feeling, listening, touching and discovering, something changes in all of us who are there.
sobre.aprendidoCol2: We’ve seen how people who didn’t know each other end up connecting in a deeply human way. How a small detail comes to hold great meaning. How we learn to trust more, to listen better and to be truly present.
sobre.aprendidoFinal: That’s why we believe the real impact of these trips isn’t only in the places we visit. It’s in the people we become when we live them together.
sobre.aprendidoNegrita: Our greatest wish is that you go home with the feeling of having lived something you’ll remember for a lifetime. Because the best trips aren’t measured by the kilometres travelled, but by what they leave inside us.
sobre.holaP1: Two Spaniards who arrived in New Zealand seven years ago with a backpack full of excitement... and who are still amazed by this country.
sobre.holaP2: We love getting up early to watch a sunrise, improvising a stop because someone heard a hidden river, laughing for hours in the van and ending the day sharing stories around a table.
sobre.holaQuoteCite: — What we’re most moved to hear
sobre.holaP3: We’re curious by nature. We love asking questions, listening to stories and discovering how each person lives in the world. Maybe that’s why Watchout came about so naturally.
sobre.equipoMoniBio: Co-founder of Watchout and guide on every trip, start to finish. She landed in New Zealand seven years ago with a backpack full of dreams, and now translates the country through story, touch and sound.
sobre.equipoMoniFotoAlt: Moni, co-founder and guide at Watchout Tours, in New Zealand
sobre.equipoSylvieBio: Co-founder of Watchout and guide on every trip, start to finish. Her father, a ski guide for blind skiers in Spain, sparked the idea that became this project.
sobre.equipoSylvieFotoAlt: Sylvie, co-founder and guide at Watchout Tours, in New Zealand
sobre.equipoNuriaBio: Nuria travelled with us on our pilot trip — 23 days across New Zealand with her husband and son. She’s an accessibility consultant and writes at Six Sense Travel, her platform on inclusive tourism. She’s now our representative in Europe.
sobre.equipoNuriaFotoAlt: Nuria smiling during her pilot trip across New Zealand with Watchout Tours
sobre.filoTitle: Five principles that guide every decision
sobre.filoFotoAlt: A Watchout Tours traveller at the top of a New Zealand mountain, with a wide landscape behind her

principios.titulo: Designed from the start, not adapted later
principios.texto: We build every trip from the very first step thinking about who travels with us.
The silence of a fjord at dawn is a luxury for every sense.
Because the sensory experience needs space and each person has their own pace.
We work with local communities, not over them.
The people who travel with us are adults who have chosen an extraordinary adventure.

sobre.cierre1: We thought we were going to show people New Zealand. And in the end it was New Zealand —and the people we’ve shared the road with— who taught us.
sobre.cierreDeseo: We hope that when you get home you won’t just remember the places you visited, but notice that you now pay attention to things that used to pass you by.
sobre.cierre2: Because perhaps that’s the best souvenir you can take with you.

privacidad.datos2: Email and/or phone (at least one, so we can reply to you)

privacidad.finalidadTitle: What we use your data for and on what basis
privacidad.finalidadText1: to respond to your enquiry and talk with you about the trip you’re interested in. Nothing more. We don’t store your data in marketing databases, we don’t send advertising or newsletters, and we don’t create profiles.
privacidad.finalidadText2: pre-contractual measures taken at your request (Art. 6.1.b GDPR) and your consent, which you give by ticking the acceptance box before submitting the form (Art. 6.1.a GDPR).
privacidad.conservacionP: Only for as long as necessary to handle your enquiry and any conversation that arises from it. If you don’t end up travelling with us, we delete your data within a maximum of 12 months from the last contact.
privacidad.destP1a: We don’t share your data with third parties. To receive the form messages we use

privacidad.destP2a: The rest of the processing takes place in New Zealand, a country with an
privacidad.destP2strong: adequacy decision from the European Commission
privacidad.destP2b: : the EU recognises that its level of data protection is equivalent to the European one.
privacidad.cookiesStrong: does not use analytics, tracking or advertising cookies
privacidad.cookiesB: . We only use essential local technical storage for the site to work (for example, an anti-spam limit on the form), which is exempt from the consent requirement. That’s why you won’t see any cookie banner.
privacidad.derP1a: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction and portability of your data. You can exercise them by writing to

privacidad.derP2a: If you believe we haven’t handled your data correctly, you can also lodge a complaint with the
privacidad.charlaDatos: If you sign up for our online talk “Discover New Zealand through the senses”, we process your name, your email, the date you choose, any question you’d like to ask us (optional) and whether you’d like to receive news about future trips (optional).
privacidad.charlaFinalidad: to manage your registration and send you the confirmation email with the Microsoft Teams link, two reminders (24 hours and 1 hour before) and a follow-up email the day after the talk. The legal basis is your own registration request (Art. 6.1.b GDPR).
privacidad.charlaNoticias: we’ll only write to you with news about our trips if you tick that box, which is optional and unticked by default. The legal basis is your consent (Art. 6.1.a GDPR), which you can withdraw at any time by writing to

privacidad.charlaProveedores: we store registrations in Supabase and send emails with Resend, which act as data processors on our behalf. Where they process data outside the European Economic Area, the transfer is covered by the safeguards provided for in the GDPR. The talk takes place on Microsoft Teams: when you join, Microsoft processes the data you enter (for example, the name you join with) under its own privacy policy.

charla.title: Discover New Zealand through the senses
charla.intro: What is it like to travel in New Zealand with blindness or low vision? Join our free talk to discover its sensory experiences, learn how we support travellers and get answers to your questions about the trip.
charla.idiomaAviso: Please note: the talk is in Spanish.

info.title: About the talk
info.mismaCharla: The talk takes place on two dates with the same content: choose whichever suits you best.
info.plataforma: Microsoft Teams. It’s an online meeting: you don’t need to sign up to Teams.

descubriras.title: What you’ll discover
items: New Zealand’s nature, sounds, flavours and Māori culture.
How we organise the trip and support blind and low-vision travellers, respecting their independence.
The main experiences of our next trip.

paraQuien.title: Who it’s for
items: Anyone interested in this kind of trip.

nosotras.title: Who we are
nosotras.p1: We’re Mónica and Sylvie, the founders of WatchOut!: two Spaniards who live in New Zealand and guide every trip, from start to finish.
nosotras.p2: The spark for the project came from Sylvie’s father, a ski guide for blind skiers in Spain. Today we design sensory trips to discover New Zealand through storytelling, touch and sound.
nosotras.p3: We’ll be joining from New Zealand, where it will be Sunday morning: 25 October and 8 November at 8:00, Auckland time.

entrar.title: How to join the talk
entrar.enlace: When you sign up, we’ll email you the Microsoft Teams link for your session. We’ll remind you again 24 hours and 1 hour before.
entrar.ordenador: join from your web browser, with no Microsoft account and nothing to install. Open the link and choose “Continue on this browser”.
entrar.movil: you’ll need the free Microsoft Teams app. Install it before the talk and join with the link as a guest.
entrar.ayuda: Need technical help before the talk? Message us and we’ll help you connect:

grabacion.title: Recording
grabacion.p: We are going to record the talk. The recording will include the voice and image of anyone who turns on their microphone or camera. If you’d rather not appear, keep them off and type your questions in the meeting chat.

final.title: Will you join us?
final.p: It’s free and all you need is an internet connection. Save your place and we’ll email you the link to join.
